title: 修复总是断开连接的问题

judgment.rationale: The report describes repeated Windows-to-Windows LAN disconnections and reconnection attempts, which likely concerns Mouse Without Borders, but it does not name the module or provide the timing, connection topology, endpoint versions, or diagnostics needed to locate the failure boundary.
evidence: The issue says a laptop and desktop on the same Wi-Fi LAN repeatedly disconnect and require reconnection.
The reporter runs PowerToys as administrator and uses Microsoft Store PowerToys 0.100.2.
The sole automated triage comment asks for an English translation and a current-version check; the issue carries Needs-Author-Feedback.
Mouse Without Borders is the PowerToys component designed for cross-PC LAN connections and has connection, socket, machine-pool, and service code.

Current and resolved Mouse Without Borders reports cover different disconnect modes, including reconnect failures, connection loss after input, cursor-related loss, service-mode loss, and network reachability; none is a sufficiently specific duplicate of this report.

Recent Mouse Without Borders history includes connection-encryption and service/file-context work, but no linked implementation or issue timeline entry covers this unspecified recurring-disconnection report.
judgment.recommended_action: Request a translated Mouse Without Borders-specific reproduction plus a fresh diagnostic archive captured immediately after a disconnect, then compare the affected endpoints and network path before proposing a code fix.

fix_assessment.rationale: No specific PowerToys connection mechanism is identified. The report could concern Mouse Without Borders transport, service mode, pairing state, Wi-Fi/network policy, or a different module, so a repository change would be speculative.

issue_context.summary: A laptop and desktop on the same Wi-Fi network reportedly disconnect repeatedly and must be reconnected, but the report does not explicitly identify the PowerToys feature or the conditions of the failure.
known_information: The report names two Windows devices, a laptop and desktop, on the same Wi-Fi LAN.
The reporter says the connection always disconnects and requires reconnection.
PowerToys 0.100.2 was installed through Microsoft Store.
No bug-report ZIP, screenshots, timing pattern, named module, or follow-up from the author is available.
The current labels are Issue-Bug, Needs-Author-Feedback, Needs-Triage, and Product-General; there is no assignee.
Mouse Without Borders is the likely cross-device feature based on the described setup, and its source includes MachinePool, SocketStuff, TCP server, and service components.
inferences: Mouse Without Borders is likely the intended feature, but the issue does not confirm this.
The repeated disconnect may occur in the connection transport, endpoint service/session lifecycle, pairing state, or local network policy; none of these is confirmed.
Because the devices are on Wi-Fi, a network transition or wireless isolation policy is plausible, but it must not be treated as the root cause without diagnostics.
issue_context.analysis: The report supplies the broad symptom but lacks the discriminator needed for a safe implementation decision. A fresh diagnostic archive immediately after failure can expose the module and connection-state evidence, while a compact translated reproduction and endpoint comparison can identify whether the failure is symmetric and whether it follows sleep, lock, Wi-Fi roaming, input crossing, or a fixed interval. The requested evidence is narrowly tied to the reported recurring connection loss and does not ask the reporter to repeat facts already supplied.
initial_investigation: Read the complete live issue body, labels, assignees, automated triage comment, and timeline; no linked work was recorded.

Searched live and resolved PowerToys issues for Mouse Without Borders disconnect and reconnect reports. Existing reports describe several distinct failure modes, including #39054, #43292, #45640, #49816, and older resolved reconnect reports, without establishing a direct duplicate.

Inspected the current Mouse Without Borders source layout and connection-related classes, including App/Class/MachinePool.cs, App/Class/SocketStuff.cs, App/Class/TcpServer.cs, App/Core/MachineStuff.cs, and App/Core/Service.cs.
Reviewed recent Mouse Without Borders history, including connection encryption changes and service/file-context changes; no current PR or commit directly matches the insufficiently scoped symptom.

Confirmed that Command Palette includes a Mouse Without Borders reconnect command, which supports treating reconnection as a module-specific state transition to capture rather than a generic application failure.

information_gaps.information: Confirmation that the affected feature is Mouse Without Borders, a short English or bilingual reproduction, and the point at which the disconnect occurs.
information_gaps.why_needed: This identifies the module and distinguishes a pairing/setup failure from a connection that drops after sleep, lock, Wi-Fi changes, input crossing, or elapsed time.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Please state whether Mouse Without Borders is the affected feature, then describe when the connection first succeeds and what happens immediately before it disconnects.

information_gaps.information: A fresh PowerToys diagnostic archive from both devices immediately after reproducing the disconnection, plus the PowerToys version on each endpoint.
information_gaps.why_needed: Connection and service logs are needed to identify which endpoint or connection stage fails and to correlate it with the reported reconnection requirement.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Immediately after the disconnect occurs, submit a comment containing /bugreport from each affected device and state which archive is from the laptop versus the desktop.

information_gaps.information: Whether both devices use the same Wi-Fi access point, and whether sleep, lock, VPN, firewall/security software, or Wi-Fi roaming occurs near the disconnect.
information_gaps.why_needed: These conditions distinguish a PowerToys connection lifecycle issue from an endpoint or network interruption without requesting private network identifiers.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Provide yes/no answers and general timing only; do not include Wi-Fi names, IP addresses, device names, or organizational network details.

comment.body: Thank you for reporting the repeated laptop-to-desktop disconnections. It sounds like Mouse Without Borders, but the report does not yet identify the connection stage that fails. Please confirm that Mouse Without Borders is the affected feature and provide a short English or bilingual description of when it disconnects (for example after sleep, lock, Wi-Fi change, moving the pointer between PCs, or after a fixed time). Immediately after reproducing the disconnect, submit a comment containing /bugreport from each affected device and state which archive is laptop versus desktop, along with the PowerToys version on each. Please also say whether both devices use the same Wi-Fi access point and whether VPN, security software, sleep, lock, or Wi-Fi roaming occurs near the failure; do not include Wi-Fi names, IP addresses, device names, or work-network details.
